paras: The lynching of Ed McCollum took place in Sheridan, the county seat of Grant County, Arkansas, around midnight on the night of October 5, 1903, when a masked mob took McCollum, a Black man, from the county jail, tied him to a tree and shot him to death. He had been jailed after he was accused of shooting and wounding a constable who tried to arrest him on a charge of assaulting another Black man. The killing was reported in Arkansas papers and in a short wire dispatch printed across the country, and a Black weekly later counted it among the year's lynchings.

According to the Pine Bluff Daily Graphic, Constable Ed M. Crutchfield tried to arrest McCollum about 11 o'clock on Friday night, October 2, on a warrant charging him with having assaulted another Black man. Other reports gave the charge as attempting to kill, or assault with intent to kill, another Black man. The Graphic said McCollum "resisted arrest and drew a gun and opened fire," wounding the officer in the arm, and the Sharp County Record reported that the wound might cost the constable his arm. No account from McCollum's side of the shooting appears in the coverage.

Reports of the arrest differ: the Graphic said McCollum was arrested Saturday morning and put in jail, while the Sharp County Record said Sheriff W. D. McDaniels arrested him later on Friday night and brought him to the Sheridan jail on Saturday night.

Around midnight on the night of October 5, a group of masked men went to the county jail at Sheridan. The Graphic put the mob at 15 to 25 men who "broke open the jail," while the Sharp County Record counted twelve or fifteen masked men who "overpowered the jailer." They took McCollum out, tied him to a tree in the courthouse yard and shot him to death, or, in the Graphic's words, "riddled his body with bullets."

The Graphic reported that "the mob did its work quietly, and few knew before daylight that the lynching had occurred." By the Sharp County Record's account the mob dispersed quickly, and the identity of its members was unknown.
No report of an inquest, arrest or prosecution of the mob appears in the coverage.

Arkansas papers carried the fullest accounts: the Pine Bluff Daily Graphic put the story on its front page on October 6 under the headline "ED McCOLLUM, COLORED, TAKEN FROM SHEIDAN JAIL BY A MOB," and the Sharp County Record printed a Sheridan dispatch on October 9 as "Lynch Law al Sheridan." A short Associated Press dispatch dated Sheridan, October 6, ran the next day in papers from Indianapolis and St. Louis to Salt Lake City, with later versions under Memphis and Sheridan datelines. The Butte Inter Mountain printed it under a "Sheridan, Wyo." dateline, and other copies turned the constable's "Davis county" into "Lewis" or "Leavis" county.

White headlines put the officer's wounding first, as in the Birmingham Age-Herald's "He Had Shot and Attempted to Kill the Town Marshal" and the Saint Paul Globe's "Colored Man Resisted Arrest and Shot Town Constable." The Indianapolis Journal headed its item "Negro Hanged to a Tree," although its text said McCollum was shot. None of the white reports commented on the mob, and by mid-October weekly roundups reduced the case to one line: McCollum was shot "for wounding an officer who tried to arrest him."

In the Black press, the American Citizen printed the same wire text on October 9 under the heading "Shot to Death by a Mob." The Chicago Broad Ax's year-end chronology of January 2, 1904, listed "Ed McCollum (colored), at Sheridan, Ark.; for wounding officer" under October in its roll of the year's lynchings, repeating the reason the white papers gave. No Black-press editorial or correspondent's account of the lynching appears in the coverage.

The papers spelled the victim's name as Ed McCollum, Ed McCullom and "E. C. Collum," and gave the officer as Constable Ed M. Crutchfield, Constable F. M. Crutchfield or Marshal F. M. Crutchfield. The two most detailed reports, both from Arkansas, also differ on the mob's size and on the arrest, and the coverage does not settle either point.

reader.title: Lynching of Ed McCollum
bases: A masked mob took McCollum from the county jail, tied him to a tree in the courthouse yard and shot him to death (A1, A15, A5).

A mob of 15 to 25 (A1) or twelve to fifteen masked men (A15) broke into or overpowered the jailer at the Sheridan jail and shot McCollum to death without legal authority; the papers tie the killing to his alleged shooting of a constable (A1, A5, A17).

The Pine Bluff Daily Graphic (A1), a Sheridan dispatch in the Sharp County Record (A15), a Little Rock Gazette special (A5) and the Associated Press wire (A2) agree on the jail seizure and shooting, while differing in details.

accounts.label: Pine Bluff Daily Graphic (Arkansas)
accounts.gist: McCollum resisted arrest and fired on Constable Ed M. Crutchfield on Friday night; arrested Saturday morning; a mob of 15 to 25 broke open the jail at midnight Monday and riddled him with bullets, working so quietly that few knew before daylight.

accounts.label: Sheridan dispatch (Sharp County Record)
accounts.gist: Sheriff W. D. McDaniels arrested 'E. C. Collum' Friday night and jailed him Saturday night; twelve or fifteen masked men overpowered the jailer and shot him in the courtyard; identities unknown.

accounts.label: Little Rock Gazette special
accounts.gist: Masked mob took McCullom from the jail and shot him; he had wounded 'Marshal F. M. Crutchfield' who sought to arrest him for assault with intent to kill.

accounts.label: Associated Press wire
accounts.gist: Masked mob took McCollum from the county jail early on October 6, tied him to a tree in the courthouse yard and shot him; he had seriously wounded Constable Crutchfield the week before.

framing.detail: Most papers ran the short AP dispatch, with headlines such as 'Negro Shot by a Mob' and 'Colored Man Resisted Arrest and Shot Town Constable' that put the officer's wounding forward as the cause; no white paper commented on the mob.
The Arkansas Graphic and Sharp County Record ran fuller local accounts ('Lynch Law al Sheridan. HOT TIME.') without editorial comment.
The American Citizen printed the wire brief 'Shot to Death by a Mob'; the Chicago Broad Ax listed the case in its year-end 'Lynchings' chronology; no editorial comment found.

conflicts.note: Spelling variants of one man; the Arkansas Graphic uses McCollum.
